metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
units.rightText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother,

units.leftText: To the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae: Grace and peace to you from God our Father. Thanksgiving and Prayer (1 Corinthians 1:4–9|1CO 1:4-9*; Philippians 1:3–11|PHP 1:3-11*)
units.rightText: to the saints and faithful brethren in Christ that are at Colossæ: Grace to you and peace from God our Father.
leftNotes: 1:2 BYZ and TR God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ

units.leftText: We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you,
units.rightText: We give thanks to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you,

units.leftText: because we have heard about your faith in Christ Jesus and your love for all the saints —
units.rightText: having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love which ye have toward all the saints,

units.leftText: the faith and love proceeding from the hope stored up for you in heaven, of which you have already heard in the word of truth, the gospel
units.rightText: because of the hope which is laid up for you in the heavens, whereof ye heard before in the word of the truth of the gospel,

units.leftText: that has come to you.
units.rightText: which is come unto you; even as it is also in all the world bearing fruit and increasing, as it doth in you also, since the day ye heard and knew the grace of God in truth;

units.leftText: You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on our behalf,
units.rightText: even as ye learned of Epaphras our beloved fellow-servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on our behalf,
leftNotes: 1:7 NE, NA, BYZ, and TR your

units.leftText: and who also informed us of your love in the Spirit.
units.rightText: who also declared unto us your love in the Spirit.

units.leftText: For this reason, since the day we heard about you, we have not stopped praying for you and asking God to fill you with the knowledge of His will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
units.rightText: For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray and make request for you, that ye may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,

units.leftText: so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord and may please Him in every way: bearing fruit in every good work, growing in the knowledge of God,
units.rightText: to walk worthily of the Lord unto all pleasing, bearing fruit in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;

units.leftText: being strengthened with all power according to His glorious might so that you may have full endurance and patience, and joyfully
units.rightText: strengthened with all power, according to the might of his glory, unto all patience and longsuffering with joy;

units.leftText: giving thanks to the Father, who has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light.
units.rightText: giving thanks unto the Father, who made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light;

units.leftText: He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son,
units.rightText: who delivered us out of the power of darkness, and translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love;

units.leftText: in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins. The Supremacy of the Son (Hebrews 1:1–14|HEB 1:1-14*)
units.rightText: in whom we have our redemption, the forgiveness of our sins:

units.leftText: The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation.
units.rightText: who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation;

units.leftText: For in Him all things were created, things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities. All things were created through Him and for Him.
units.rightText: for in him were all things created, in the heavens and upon the earth, things visible and things invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers; all things have been created through him, and unto him;

units.leftText: He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
units.rightText: and he is before all things, and in him all things consist.

units.leftText: And He is the head of the body, the church; He is the beginning and firstborn from among the dead, so that in all things He may have preeminence.
units.rightText: And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.

units.leftText: For God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him,
units.rightText: For it was the good pleasure of the Father that in him should all the fulness dwell;

units.leftText: and through Him to reconcile to Himself all things, whether things on earth or things in heaven, by making peace through the blood of His cross.
units.rightText: and through him to reconcile all things unto himself, having made peace through the blood of his cross; through him, I say, whether things upon the earth, or things in the heavens.

units.leftText: Once you were alienated from God and were hostile in your minds, engaging in evil deeds.
units.rightText: And you, being in time past alienated and enemies in your mind in your evil works,

units.leftText: But now He has reconciled you by Christ’s physical body through death to present you holy, unblemished, and blameless in His presence —
units.rightText: yet now hath he reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and without blemish and unreproveable before him:

units.leftText: if indeed you continue in your faith, established and firm, not moved from the hope of the gospel you heard, which has been proclaimed to every creature under heaven, and of which I, Paul, have become a servant. Paul’s Suffering for the Church (2 Corinthians 11:16–33|2CO 11:16-33*)
units.rightText: if so be that ye continue in the faith, grounded and stedfast, and not moved away from the hope of the gospel which ye heard, which was preached in all creation under heaven; whereof I Paul was made a minister.

units.leftText: Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and I fill up in my flesh what is lacking in regard to Christ’s afflictions for the sake of His body, which is the church.
units.rightText: Now I rejoice in my sufferings for your sake, and fill up on my part that which is lacking of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body’s sake, which is the church;

units.leftText: I became its servant by the commission God gave me to fully proclaim to you the word of God,
units.rightText: whereof I was made a minister, according to the dispensation of God which was given me to you-ward, to fulfil the word of God,

units.leftText: the mystery that was hidden for ages and generations but is now revealed to His saints.
units.rightText: even the mystery which hath been hid for ages and generations: but now hath it been manifested to his saints,

units.leftText: To them God has chosen to make known among the Gentiles the glorious riches of this mystery, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
units.rightText: to whom God was pleased to make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory:

units.leftText: We proclaim Him, admonishing and teaching everyone with all wisdom, so that we may present everyone perfect in Christ.
units.rightText: whom we proclaim, admonishing every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, that we may present every man perfect in Christ;

units.leftText: To this end I also labor, striving with all His energy working powerfully within me.
units.rightText: whereunto I labor also, striving according to his working, which worketh in me mightily.

units.leftText: For I want you to know how much I am struggling for you and for those at Laodicea, and for all who have not met me face to face,
units.rightText: For I would have you know how greatly I strive for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh;

units.leftText: that they may be encouraged in heart, knit together in love, and filled with the full riches of complete understanding, so that they may know the mystery of God, namely Christ,
units.rightText: that their hearts may be comforted, they being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, that they may know the mystery of God, even Christ,
leftNotes: 2:2 Literally the mystery of God: Christ

units.leftText: in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
units.rightText: in whom are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden.

units.leftText: I say this so that no one will deceive you by smooth rhetoric.
units.rightText: This I say, that no one may delude you with persuasiveness of speech.

units.leftText: For although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I delight to see your orderly condition and firm faith in Christ. Alive with Christ (Ephesians 2:1–10|EPH 2:1-10*)
units.rightText: For though I am absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order, and the stedfastness of your faith in Christ.

units.leftText: Therefore, just as you have received Christ Jesus as Lord, continue to walk in Him,
units.rightText: As therefore ye received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him,

units.leftText: rooted and built up in Him, established in the faith as you were taught, and overflowing with thankfulness.
units.rightText: rooted and builded up in him, and established in your faith, even as ye were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.

units.leftText: See to it that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deception, which are based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world rather than on Christ.
units.rightText: Take heed lest there shall be any one that maketh spoil of you through his philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ:

units.leftText: For in Christ all the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form.
units.rightText: for in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily,

units.leftText: And you have been made complete in Christ, who is the head over every ruler and authority.
units.rightText: and in him ye are made full, who is the head of all principality and power:

units.leftText: In Him you were also circumcised, in the putting off of your sinful nature, with the circumcision performed by Christ and not by human hands.
units.rightText: in whom ye were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in the putting off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ;
leftNotes: 2:11 Literally in the cutting away of the body of the flesh, by the circumcision of Christ

units.leftText: And having been buried with Him in baptism, you were raised with Him through your faith in the power of God, who raised Him from the dead.
units.rightText: having been buried with him in baptism, wherein ye were also raised with him through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.

units.leftText: When you were dead in your trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your sinful nature, God made you alive with Christ. He forgave us all our trespasses,
units.rightText: And you, being dead through your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, you, I say, did he make alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses;

units.leftText: having canceled the debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us. He took it away, nailing it to the cross!
units.rightText: having blotted out the bond written in ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us: and he hath taken it out of the way, nailing it to the cross;

units.leftText: And having disarmed the powers and authorities, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross.
units.rightText: having despoiled the principalities and the powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it.

units.leftText: Therefore let no one judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a feast, a New Moon, or a Sabbath.
units.rightText: Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of a feast day or a new moon or a sabbath day:

units.leftText: These are a shadow of the things to come, but the body that casts it belongs to Christ.
units.rightText: which are a shadow of the things to come; but the body is Christ’s.
leftNotes: 2:17 Literally but the body is of the Christ

units.leftText: Do not let anyone who delights in false humility and the worship of angels disqualify you with speculation about what he has seen. Such a person is puffed up without basis by his unspiritual mind.
units.rightText: Let no man rob you of your prize by a voluntary humility and worshipping of the angels, dwelling in the things which he hath seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind,

units.leftText: He has lost connection to the head, from whom the whole body, supported and knit together by its joints and ligaments, grows as God causes it to grow.
units.rightText: and not holding fast the Head, from whom all the body, being supplied and knit together through the joints and bands, increaseth with the increase of God.

units.leftText: If you have died with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world, why, as though you still belonged to the world, do you submit to its regulations:
units.rightText: If ye died with Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as though living in the world, do ye subject yourselves to ordinances,

units.leftText: “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!”?
units.rightText: Handle not, nor taste, nor touch

units.leftText: These will all perish with use, because they are based on human commands and teachings.
units.rightText: (all which things are to perish with the using), after the precepts and doctrines of men?

units.leftText: Such restrictions indeed have an appearance of wisdom, with their self-prescribed worship, their false humility, and their harsh treatment of the body; but they are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.
units.rightText: Which things have indeed a show of wisdom in will-worship, and humility, and severity to the body; but are not of any value against the indulgence of the flesh.

units.leftText: Therefore, since you have been raised with Christ, strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
units.rightText: If then ye were raised together with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated on the right hand of God.

units.leftText: Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things.
units.rightText: Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are upon the earth.

units.leftText: For you died, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.
units.rightText: For ye died, and your life is hid with Christ in God.

units.leftText: When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.
units.rightText: When Christ, who is our life, shall be manifested, then shall ye also with him be manifested in glory.
leftNotes: 3:4 NE, WH, BYZ, and TR our

units.leftText: Put to death, therefore, the components of your earthly nature: sexual immorality, impurity, lust, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.
units.rightText: Put to death therefore your members which are upon the earth: fornication, uncleanness, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry;

units.leftText: Because of these, the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.
units.rightText: for which things’ sake cometh the wrath of God upon the sons of disobedience:
leftNotes: 3:6 NE, WH, and Tischendorf do not include on the sons of disobedience.

units.leftText: When you lived among them, you also used to walk in these ways.
units.rightText: wherein ye also once walked, when ye lived in these things;

units.leftText: But now you must put aside all such things as these: anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language from your lips.
units.rightText: but now do ye also put them all away: anger, wrath, malice, railing, shameful speaking out of your mouth:

units.leftText: Do not lie to one another, since you have taken off the old self with its practices,
units.rightText: lie not one to another; seeing that ye have put off the old man with his doings,

units.leftText: and have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator.
units.rightText: and have put on the new man, that is being renewed unto knowledge after the image of him that created him:

units.leftText: Here there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free, but Christ is all and is in all.
units.rightText: where there cannot be Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, bondman, freeman; but Christ is all, and in all.

units.leftText: Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
units.rightText: Put on therefore, as God’s elect, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, meekness, longsuffering;

units.leftText: Bear with one another and forgive any complaint you may have against someone else. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
units.rightText: forbearing one another, and forgiving each other, if any man have a complaint against any; even as the Lord forgave you, so also do ye:

units.leftText: And over all these virtues put on love, which is the bond of perfect unity.
units.rightText: and above all these things put on love, which is the bond of perfectness.

units.leftText: Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, for to this you were called as members of one body. And be thankful.
units.rightText: And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to the which also ye were called in one body; and be ye thankful.

units.leftText: Let the word of Christ richly dwell within you as you teach and admonish one another with all wisdom, and as you sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude in your hearts to God.
units.rightText: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts unto God.

units.leftText: And whatever you do, in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him. Christian Households (Ephesians 6:1–4|EPH 6:1-4*)
units.rightText: And whatsoever ye do, in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.

units.leftText: Wives, submit to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
units.rightText: Wives, be in subjection to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.

units.leftText: Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.
units.rightText: Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them.

units.leftText: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
units.rightText: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well-pleasing in the Lord.

units.leftText: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so they will not become discouraged. Serving with Honor (Ephesians 6:5–9|EPH 6:5-9*; 1 Timothy 6:1–2|1TI 6:1-2*)
units.rightText: Fathers, provoke not your children, that they be not discouraged.

units.leftText: Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only to please them while they are watching, but with sincerity of heart and fear of the Lord.
units.rightText: Servants, obey in all things them that are your masters according to the flesh; not with eye-service, as men-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing the Lord:

units.leftText: Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, as for the Lord and not for men,
units.rightText: whatsoever ye do, work heartily, as unto the Lord, and not unto men;

units.leftText: because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward. It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
units.rightText: knowing that from the Lord ye shall receive the recompense of the inheritance: ye serve the Lord Christ.

units.leftText: Whoever does wrong will be repaid for his wrong, and there is no favoritism.
units.rightText: For he that doeth wrong shall receive again for the wrong that he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.

units.leftText: Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.
units.rightText: Masters, render unto your servants that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.

units.leftText: Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful,
units.rightText: Continue stedfastly in prayer, watching therein with thanksgiving;

units.leftText: as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.
units.rightText: withal praying for us also, that God may open unto us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds;

units.leftText: Pray that I may declare it clearly, as I should.
units.rightText: that I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak.

units.leftText: Act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time.
units.rightText: Walk in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time.

units.leftText: Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone. Greetings from Paul’s Fellow Workers (Romans 16:21–23|ROM 16:21-23*)
units.rightText: Let your speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer each one.

units.leftText: Tychicus will tell you all the news about me. He is a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord.
units.rightText: All my affairs shall Tychicus make known unto you, the beloved brother and faithful minister and fellow-servant in the Lord:

units.leftText: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know about us, and that he may encourage your hearts.
units.rightText: whom I have sent unto you for this very purpose, that ye may know our state, and that he may comfort your hearts;

units.leftText: With him I am sending Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you about everything here.
units.rightText: together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things that are done here.

units.leftText: My fellow prisoner Aristarchus sends you greetings, as does Mark the cousin of Barnabas. You have already received instructions about him: If he comes to you, welcome him.
units.rightText: Aristarchus my fellow-prisoner saluteth you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas (touching whom ye received commandments; if he come unto you, receive him),

units.leftText: Jesus, who is called Justus, also sends greetings. These are the only Jews among my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.
units.rightText: and Jesus that is called Justus, who are of the circumcision: these only are my fellow-workers unto the kingdom of God, men that have been a comfort unto me.

units.leftText: Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God.
units.rightText: Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, saluteth you, always striving for you in his prayers, that ye may stand perfect and fully assured in all the will of God.

units.leftText: For I testify about him that he goes to great pains for you and for those at Laodicea and Hierapolis.
units.rightText: For I bear him witness, that he hath much labor for you, and for them in Laodicea, and for them in Hierapolis.

units.leftText: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send you greetings. Signature and Final Instructions (1 Corinthians 16:19–24|1CO 16:19-24*; 2 Thessalonians 3:16–18|2TH 3:16-18*)
units.rightText: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas salute you.

units.leftText: Greet the brothers in Laodicea, as well as Nympha and the church that meets at her house.
units.rightText: Salute the brethren that are in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church that is in their house.

units.leftText: After this letter has been read among you, make sure that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you in turn read the letter from Laodicea.
units.rightText: And when this epistle hath been read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that ye also read the epistle from Laodicea.

units.leftText: Tell Archippus: “See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord.”
units.rightText: And say to Archippus, Take heed to the ministry which thou hast received in the Lord, that thou fulfil it.

units.leftText: This greeting is in my own hand — Paul. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
units.rightText: The salutation of me Paul with mine own hand. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you.
